Summary: The hoard comprised 7 bronzes coins from the reign of Nero, dated between AD 67-68, which may have belonged to a Roman soldier during the First Jewish War.
Comment: "The first possibility is that the hoard is somehow related to the late first-century burials even though it was not deposited in the graves and despite the coins’ date some decades earlier than the other grave goods. The second would be that there was  fighting in the underground passageway and the hoard was lost by a soldier there. The third possibility, perhaps the most likely, is that a Roman soldier intentionally hid the coins in this underground location, which he would be able to locate easily after the fighting was over. In any event, the owner of the small hoard never retrieved the coins, either because he did not deposit them but lost them and did not know where to  find them, or because he was unable to retrieve them due to the sudden transfer of his unit elsewhere, or because he was wounded or worse. Another possibility is that the owner thought the small value of the deposit not worth the effort to return to Tell el-Ful to retrieve it" (Ariel et al. 2014, 150-151).
